title: Federal preemption in the assigned procedural settings
shortTitle: Federal preemption in the assigned procedural settings
summary: Preemption occurs when controlling federal law displaces a conflicting state rule. The course encounters it in arbitration, jurisdictional characterization, and enforcement of federal rights.
notes: An ordinary federal defense generally does not itself create federal-question jurisdiction. Do not confuse preemption on the merits with the special removal doctrines discussed in the jurisdiction notes.

sections.Meaning: Preemption occurs when controlling federal law displaces a conflicting state rule. The course encounters it in arbitration, jurisdictional characterization, and enforcement of federal rights.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the federal source, the state rule, and the type of conflict actually asserted. In Concepcion, the majority considered the change from bilateral to class arbitration inconsistent with the federal arbitration framework.
